## Breaking change: `Review.id` is now the raw store identifier

`Review.id` no longer carries a `"<source>-"` prefix.

```python
# 0.4.0
review.id   # "googleplay_scraper-abc123"

# 0.5.0
review.id   # "abc123"
```

**Why:** the prefix duplicated `Review.source`, and it broke replies. Consumers pass `id` to the store reply APIs — Google Play `androidpublisher` `reviews.reply` and App Store Connect `customerReviewResponses` — and both reject a prefixed id, so every reply attempt failed on both platforms.

### If you upgrade

- **Reading provenance from the prefix?** Use `review.source` instead — it is a typed `Literal` (`appstore_scraper`, `appstore_official`, `googleplay_scraper`, `googleplay_official`).
- **Stored ids from 0.4.x?** They are still prefixed in your data. Strip the leading `"<source>-"` on read, or re-fetch.
- **Deduplicating on `id` alone?** Key on `(store, source, id)` instead. See below.

### Don't assume ids are comparable across sources

Treat an `id` as unique within a `(store, source)` pair and key deduplication on `(store, source, id)`.

On the App Store the two providers definitely use different identifier spaces: RSS ids are numeric (`14357217033`) while Connect `customerReviews.id` is opaque, and Apple exposes no mapping between them. So the same review fetched via `appstore_scraper` and `appstore_official` carries different ids — that was true before this release too; the prefix merely hid it behind a uniqueness guarantee it was not actually providing.

Google Play appears to use a single identifier space across both providers, so ids there may well match.

Replying to reviews is outside this package, but for App Store Connect `customerReviewResponses` needs a Connect `customerReviews.id` — an `appstore_scraper` id will not work.
